up.note: For Boolean $f$ the unique real multilinear representation has integer coefficients (they are the Mobius / inclusion-exclusion coefficients $\sum_{S\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|S|}f(S)$). Reducing them mod $p$ gives a multilinear polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_p$ that still agrees with $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, of no larger degree.

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\deg_p(f) \le \deg(f)\)
    For Boolean $f$ the unique real multilinear representation has integer coefficients (they are the Mobius / inclusion-exclusion coefficients $\sum_{S\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|S|}f(S)$). Reducing them mod $p$ gives a multilinear polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_p$ that still agrees with $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, of no larger degree.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\deg(\mathrm{PARITY}_n) = n \text{ while } \deg_2(\mathrm{PARITY}_n) = 1\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\)
    The extreme case: mod $2$, parity is the linear form $\sum_i x_i$. Read the other way, no bound on $\deg$ in terms of $\deg_2$ exists.
see also: \(\deg_p(f)\), \(\deg_2(f)\), \(\deg(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/11-lp-and-lower-bound-methods.yaml

other_lo.tex: \deg_p(\oplus_n) = n \ \text{ for every odd prime } p, \quad \mathrm{spar}(\oplus_n) = 1
other_lo.note:
Fourier sparsity is a statement about the *real* representation and says nothing
about representations over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Parity is the extreme case in both
directions at once: a single Fourier coefficient, but over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with
$p$ odd it needs full degree, $\tfrac12\big(1 - \prod_i (1-2x_i)\big)$ being the
only representation. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ the two collapse to $\deg_2 = 1$,
which is why the value string for [[PARITY]] has to split on $p$.
